tasks.title: Create the structured S25 room-scan test matrix
tasks.phase: Scanner Evidence — Make Tracking Failures Observable
tasks.notes: Define repeatable cases for small/large rooms, plain walls, textured walls, reflective floors, low light.

prep.what: Define a repeatable test matrix covering every failure mode the S25 scanner encounters — the document every Phase 2 fix references to prove it works.
prep.understand: ARCore tracking degrades predictably: plain walls have no visual features for SLAM, reflective floors cause false plane detections, large rooms exceed depth sensor range. Without a structured matrix you can't reproduce a failure reliably or verify a fix worked. This is the ground-truth doc — 30 minutes now saves hours of debugging per Phase 2 task.
approach: List the known failure modes from p1t0 notes: plain walls, reflective floors, low light, large rooms (>6m), excessive motion, S25-specific depth sensor edge cases

Define 10-12 matrix entries across dimensions: room size (small/large), wall texture (plain/textured), floor type (reflective/matte), lighting (bright/dim), scan path (clockwise / interrupted / restarted after loss)
For each entry: setup steps, expected behavior, failure indicators, which ARCore metric to watch (`TrackingState`, plane count, depth availability, corner rejection reason)
Add 4-6 pure-geometry fixture test cases: wall intersection correctness, endpoint clearance, loop closure gap, coordinate transform round-trip
resources: Samsung S25 camera spec and ARCore configuration docs
Existing `tests/` directory in the tomato-android repo

tasks.title: Build on-device scan diagnostics and session export
tasks.phase: Scanner Evidence — Make Tracking Failures Observable
tasks.notes: Record tracking state, plane/depth availability, camera pose, locked-corner samples, rejection reasons.

prep.what: Add a developer debug overlay + session log export so you can see exactly what ARCore is doing in real time and export structured data from any failed scan.
prep.understand: Right now when the scanner drops a corner or loses tracking, you are debugging blind — no signal about which ARCore metric failed or why a corner was rejected. Every Phase 2 stabilization fix starts from reading a session log. Build the overlay first (real-time during scanning), then the export (structured post-scan analysis). Both are required for Phase 2 to be verifiable.
approach: Add `DebugModeManager` (shake-to-toggle) with a floating overlay card: ARCore `TrackingState`, depth buffer status, active plane count, current corner-lock confidence score, last 3 corner rejection reasons with timestamps

Build `ScanSession` data class with a list of `ScanEvent` entries (timestamp, type: CORNER_ATTEMPT / CORNER_LOCKED / CORNER_REJECTED / TRACKING_LOST / PLANE_DETECTED, metadata map) — appended on every scanner state change
On scan end or explicit export tap: serialize session to JSON, share via `ShareCompat.IntentBuilder` with `application/json` MIME type
Smoke test on S25 in a plain-wall room: confirm the overlay shows `TrackingState.PAUSED` and rejection events appear with correct types in the exported JSON
resources: Existing scanner state machine in `app/src/main/java/` — hook events there

tasks.title: Build Contact page
tasks.notes: Submission stubs to local API route for now. Source: `reference/content/contact-us.md`.

prep.what: Build the `/contact` page with a form that submits to a local stub API route — no real email delivery yet, just returns 200 and shows a success state.
prep.understand: Submission chain: React controlled form → `fetch('/api/contact', { method: 'POST', body: JSON.stringify(data) })` → Next.js route handler at `app/api/contact/route.ts` that logs the payload and returns `{ ok: true }`. The page shows an inline success message on submit without a full redirect. Keep the form short (name, email, message + any fields from the content file).
approach: Read `reference/content/contact-us.md` for copy, field names, and any section structure
Create `app/api/contact/route.ts` — POST handler that parses JSON body, logs it, returns `NextResponse.json({ ok: true })`
Create `app/contact/page.tsx` as a client component with controlled inputs and `onSubmit` handler that calls the API and sets a success boolean in state
Add a Contact link to the footer/nav; run `npx tsc --noEmit` to confirm no TypeScript errors
resources: Existing API routes in `app/api/` for pattern reference
